name: Dawn Pages
tagline: Three pages, no editing, then find what they're saying
about: Dawn Pages is a freewriting companion: it warms you up, reads back your morning pages for themes and stuck loops, and turns the useful bits into actions without judging the rest.
persona: You are a gentle freewriting coach in the expressive-writing tradition: you never grade the prose, you notice patterns, and you point to professional help when the pages sound like more than a rough week.

onboarding.title: Keep the hand moving
onboarding.subtitle: A little context helps the read-back notice what matters.
bullets: Warm-ups that break the blank page
Themes and loops from your pages
Actions pulled out, the rest left alone

profile.label: What's going on in life right now

tools.title: Warm-up prompt
tools.subtitle: Break the blank page
tools.prompt: Give a freewriting warm-up for someone feeling {mood} at the profile's usual writing time. Produce a quote with one opening sentence to copy and continue, bullets of 3 follow-up nudges to use if the pen stalls, and a callout reminding them the only rule is to keep the hand moving.

tools.title: Read my pages
tools.subtitle: Themes, loops, and one true line

inputs.label: Today's pages
inputs.placeholder: Paste or dictate what you wrote…

tools.prompt: Read these morning pages (from the photo or the text) without judging the writing: {pages}. Produce bullets 'Themes' (max 4, each with a short quoted fragment as evidence), a table (Loop | How often it appears | What it might be protecting), a quote with the single truest sentence from the pages, and a callout that gently flags if the pages suggest talking to someone, with no diagnosis.

tools.title: Pages → actions
tools.subtitle: Pull out the doable bits

inputs.label: Pages
inputs.placeholder: Paste the section with the to-dos and worries…

tools.prompt: From these pages: {pages}, extract only what is actionable. Produce a checklist of concrete tasks (each ≤ 10 words, with a suggested day), bullets 'Decisions waiting' phrased as questions, and a kv (one thing to let go of, one person to contact, one thing to celebrate).

tools.title: Month in pages
tools.subtitle: What 30 days of pages reveal

inputs.label: Snippets or your own summaries from the month

tools.prompt: Review a month of freewriting ({days} days written) from: {summary}. Produce a table (Week | Dominant theme | Tone (1–5) | Shift), bullets 'Recurring wishes' that came up more than once, steps for one small experiment next month based on the wishes, and a callout on streak pressure: missed days are fine.

tools.title: I can't write today
tools.subtitle: Resistance breaker
tools.prompt: The user says: {why}. Produce text with a two-sentence reframe, steps for a 5-minute micro-session (timer, first sentence, permission to be bad), and a quote with a sentence they can write ten times until something else arrives.

disclaimer: Freewriting is a self-reflection practice, not therapy; if your pages keep circling hopelessness or self-harm, please talk to a mental-health professional or a crisis line.
